chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from some of his family members, who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not grant Hakim ibn Hizam permission to engage in trade until he guaranteed to him the acceptance of returns by the regretful buyer, the respite for the insolvent, and taking the due right in full or in part.

key_terms.إِقَالَةَ النَّادِمِ: Acceptance of returns by the regretful buyer

ai.seo_question: What ethical conditions did the Prophet impose on Hakim ibn Hizam for trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) specific ethical stipulations for Hakim ibn Hizam, emphasizing that commercial activity must be grounded in social justice. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Iqala' (voluntary return of goods) and 'Inzar al-Mu'sir' (grace for the insolvent) as essential components of a fair market, ensuring that trade serves the community rather than merely accumulating wealth. These conditions reflect the broader Islamic principle that economic transactions are acts of worship when conducted with integrity and compassion.
